verdicts.argument: The Biktarvy IRA selection is a public January 2026 headline and sits inside the case's starter thread (how long the HIV franchise can hold). The claimed 'new' part, spillover into Medicaid rebates and 340B ceiling prices, is not new. The FY2024 10-K already said Medicare negotiation 'could also affect the Medicaid rebate obligations and the ceiling prices charged to covered entities under Section 340B ... if such prices are lower than the Medicaid Best Price' (GILD:10k_FY2024.md p.20, index page 20). The same sentence appears in the 10-Qs from 2024Q3 onward (GILD:companies/GILD/10q_2024Q3.md p.40). The FY2025 10-K (p.20) only changes 'could' to 'may also lead to' once Biktarvy was named. The 340B shift from 'limits the prices we may charge' (GILD:10k_FY2024.md p.21) to 'pervasive violations' (GILD:10k_FY2025.md p.21) is real wording drift, but analysts asked about it directly on calls: Alex Hammond (Wolfe) asked about 340B channel mix and Johanna Mercier replied that 340B had grown 'in every quarter from 2024 into 2025' and named duplicate discounts (GILD:companies/GILD/transcripts/2025Q1_transcript.md p.18, grade C). Mercier also said in 2024Q3 that 340B growth 'can impact the Medicaid patient population' (2024Q3_transcript p.18, grade C). Any IRA model built on Medicaid best price already includes the spillover by statute.
verdicts.correction: At most a narrow language-drift note: the FY2025 10-K hardens the 340B wording to 'pervasive violations' and 'out of scope percentage of sales.' It does not support a claim that Gilead newly disclosed IRA spillover.

verdicts.argument: The substance is the starter thread. The case appendix frames Gilead as 'A dominant HIV franchise, and how long that dominance can hold', and the shift to long-acting therapy is the main way that dominance could erode. Gilead says this openly. Long-acting HIV was already strategic priority (ii) in the FY2024 10-K (GILD:10k_FY2024.md p.38: '(i) maximize near-term revenue growth; (ii) maximize impact of long-acting'), so the FY2025 change is a reordering, not a new strategy. The refreshed priorities are printed on page 2 and page 31 of the 2026 proxy (GILD:companies/GILD/proxy_2026.md). Management talks up the long-acting pipeline on every call (2025Q3 grade A p.6; 2026Q1 and 2026Q2 grade C). GSK publicly says long-acting drugs drove more than 75% of its HIV growth (GSK annual report 2025 p.40, cited by the reader). The deleted risk-factor sentence is the only part a skim would miss, and it carries no number.
verdicts.correction: Keep it only as a supporting language-drift footnote to a quantified finding: the 'nucleoside-based therapeutics do not remain the preferred regimen' risk factor appears through 10-K FY2024 p.18 and 10-Q 2025Q1 p.33, then disappears. It cannot stand on its own as a finding.

verdicts.argument: The 10-K's own GTN table prints the headline: '% of gross product sales 41 % 38 % 250 bps', and it attributes the rise to Part D redesign (GILD:10k_FY2025.md p.41). The reader's 'roughly $327M unexplained' depends on comparing the $1.227B rate effect with the ~$900M HIV-only Part D figure. Management gave a company-wide number in two places. The FY2024 Q4 call: 'Medicare Part D reform is expected to impact our revenue by approximately $1.1 billion, including $900 million in HIV' (CFO Andrew Dickinson, GILD:companies/GILD/transcripts/2024Q4_transcript.md p.10, grade C). The 2025Q4 earnings slides: 'Excluding an estimated $1.1 billion in Part D Redesign headwinds, total product sales +5%' (GILD:presentations/2025Q4_earnings_slides.md p.25). Against $1.1B the residual falls to about $127M, roughly 0.4% of revenue. On the claimed dropped split: the FY2025 10-K still discloses 'rebates and chargebacks of $17.5 billion and $15.5 billion' (p.41 footnote 1), so the split is still there in dollars. The ~$900M HIV headwind also appears on the grade-A 2025Q3 call (p.1, p.3, p.9) and the 2025Q3 slides p.25.
verdicts.correction: Narrow claim: GTN rose about 250 bps, and roughly 90% of that is the Part D redesign Gilead itself quantified at about $1.1B. The unexplained remainder is about $0.1B. The list-price comparison (Biktarvy WAC +5.9% vs Dovato +4.0%) is the only piece not in company materials, and it is small.

verdicts.argument: This survives the obviousness test. Index searches for 'pre-commercial inventory' and 'Trodelvy manufacturing process inventory' return only the footnotes: 10-K FY2025 p.80 ($613M), 10-Q 2026Q1 p.18 ($638M) and 10-Q 2026Q2 p.21 ($568M). Nothing comes up in any transcript, earnings release or slide deck. The analyst_topics table shows zero analyst questions on inventory/channel in the 2026Q1 call, and the one 2026Q2 hit is about Yeztugo compliance, not Gilead's own inventory. Two points cut against it. First, the 10-K MD&A says the cash-flow decline was 'primarily due to higher inventory build-up ... as well as unfavorable timing of accounts receivable collections' (GILD:10k_FY2025.md p.46). So the build is plainly stated in the filing, though not in a release or on a call. Second, the ASCENT-07 tie-in is weak. The miss was public (10-K p.38; 8-K 2026-02-10 p.4), Trodelvy grew 37% in Q1 2026 (2026Q1 call, grade C), and first-line TNBC filings are pending. The pre-commercial lot more plausibly supports new-process capacity for the first-line TNBC launch than an indication that failed.
verdicts.correction: Reframe: $613M (now $568M) of Trodelvy inventory is capitalized on a manufacturing process FDA has not approved, about 41% of a year of Trodelvy sales, and is disclosed only in a footnote. Its recovery depends on approval of the process, not on ASCENT-07. Drop the ASCENT-07 causal link. Say that the MD&A acknowledges the inventory build but never sizes the Trodelvy portion.

verdicts.argument: Both the press release and the call state this plainly. The 2025-10-30 release puts it in a top bullet: 'royalty, contract and other revenues increased by approximately $400 million ... primarily driven by revenue related to a previous sale of intellectual property not expected to reoccur' (GILD:earnings/2025-10-30_exhibit991earningspressrel.md p.1). On the grade-A 2025Q3 call, CFO Andrew Dickinson said: 'This relates to an IP asset sale from 2018 ... This is a non-recurring accounting item and does not reflect cash received', and 'Excluding the $400 million non-recurring other revenue, non-GAAP diluted EPS would have been $2.22' (GILD:companies/GILD/transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p.9). That gives investors the exact ex-item EPS the reader says they are not given. The Q2 2026 recurrence is also in the release ('Higher royalty, contract and other revenues related to a previous sale of intellectual property', 8-K 2026-08-04 p.1), and the Q2 2026 call says 'Other revenue of $176 million included $156 million related to an increase in future estimated royalties associated with the prior IP asset sale. This is a nonrecurring and noncash item' (GILD:transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p.1, grade C). Consensus watchers saw it: I/B/E/S Q3 2025 actual is 2.47 (ibes_actuals.csv).
verdicts.correction: Only a minor residue survives: 'not expected to reoccur' in Q3 2025 was followed by a second $156M true-up in Q2 2026. Management flagged that one too, so it is not hidden.

verdicts.argument: Management gave the reordered drivers in prepared remarks, on the slide, and in the release. The Q2 2026 slide says 'YoY driven by higher average realized price due to channel mix, in addition to inventory build and higher demand' and 'QoQ ... partially offset by lower demand due to market dynamics' (GILD:presentations/2026Q2_earnings_slides.md p.9). The Q2 2026 call script reads the same and adds 'a greater-than-expected impact associated with changes in the Affordable Care Act ... we did see a slowing in HIV treatment market growth' (GILD:transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p.1, grade C). Courtney Breen asked directly about volume versus 'mix and other pricing dynamics' for Biktarvy on that call and got an answer (same page). The 8-K release has the same driver order (GILD:earnings/2026-08-04_exhibit991earningspressrel.md p.2). The ~2% HIV policy headwind from ACA subsidies and MFN Medicaid was guided on the 2025Q4 slides (p.12). Consensus is above product-sales guidance (consensus_vs_guidance.csv: FY2026 mean $30,682M vs guide $30,100-30,400M), so the Street is not discounting the price-led growth.
verdicts.correction: Only the contrast with the October 2025 'real demand-driven growth' quote (Johanna Mercier, grade A, 2025Q3 p.12) is not restated elsewhere. That is a rhetorical point, not a finding.

verdicts.argument: The core advantage, twice-yearly dosing versus Apretude, is the headline of Gilead's FDA approval press release ('the first and only twice-yearly', GILD:policy/press_2025-06-18_yeztugo_fda_approval.md p.1) and the main pitch of every PrEP discussion on the calls. The warnings and contraindications contrast comes from reading two labels side by side. That is required case work, not a hidden signal. The non-obvious twist, that Gilead is 'discounting the label advantage away', is contradicted by management: on the Q2 2026 call, HIV growth including 'Descovy and Yeztugo in PrEP' was 'driven by higher average realized price and higher demand' (GILD:transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p.1, grade C). A -0.7% Part B ASP drift over a launch year is noise. ASP lags and reflects launch-period discounting under buy-and-bill, which analysts asked about on the grade-A 2025Q3 call (p.14).
verdicts.correction: Use this as product-comparison material, not a finding. If kept, state only that Yeztugo's Part B ASP per mg was flat to slightly down while Apretude's rose 3.7% from 2025Q4 to 2026Q4 (partb_asp_quarterly.csv), and do not draw a pricing-strategy conclusion from it.

verdicts.argument: This survives the obviousness test. Biktarvy label v19 restricts treatment-experienced use to virologically suppressed patients (biktarvy:drugs/biktarvy/label_v19.md p.1). Label v22 (2025-08-08) adds 'with an antiretroviral treatment history and not virologically suppressed' (label_v22.md p.1; drug:biktarvy:label_sections.md p.2, section 14.3 p.62). Searching 'Biktarvy label expanded' finds only the 2024 M184V expansion, which was press-released (8-K 2024-04-25 p.3; 10-K FY2024 p.8). I found no release, slide, 10-K FY2025 key-event line or call mention of the August 2025 expansion, and the grade-A 2025Q3 call does not raise it. Dovato's and Cabenuva's indications do require suppression with no history of treatment failure, as the reader quotes. The weakness is materiality, not obviousness: the reader cannot size the subgroup, and naive patients are on-label for every regimen.
verdicts.correction: Present it as a quiet label widening that underpins Biktarvy's share in the viremic, treatment-experienced segment. Do not present it as a revenue driver.

verdicts.argument: Each of the three legs is either obvious or wrong. (1) Biktarvy's single-drug IRA concentration is the starter thread plus the January 2026 selection headline. (2) Low tariff exposure was said plainly by Daniel O'Day on the grade-A 2025Q3 call ('We recognize more than 80% of our IP in the United States', p.19), and the reader concedes it is 'already priced as a positive.' (3) The 'only one' repatriation claim is false. The White House fact sheet on the December 2025 deals says 'The agreements require the nine companies to repatriate increased foreign revenue on existing products', and those nine include Merck, BMS and Amgen (policy_gov:policy_gov/wh/wh_fact_sheet_2025-12-19_nine_deals_mrk_bmy_amgn_gild.md p.1). Merck's FY2025 10-K says it 'agreed to repatriate and share with the Federal government a portion of foreign revenue' (MRK:10k_FY2025.md p.54; also MRK:10q_2026Q1.md p.30). The term is standard, and policy_exposure.csv shows it for GILD only because of a coverage gap in that table.
verdicts.correction: Drop the uniqueness claim. If a peer-contrast row is needed, use the IRA share of revenue (Biktarvy 48.7% vs NVO 79.9%, BMY 43.3%) and label it as context, not a finding.

verdicts.argument: Biktarvy vs Dovato/Cabenuva is the competitive set the case hands every Gilead team, so choosing the product earns nothing on its own. The fine-print edge it rests on, the August 2025 widening to treatment-experienced patients who are not suppressed (c08), is not in any release, slide or call I could find (see c08 pages). That gives the comparison one point other teams are unlikely to have. The HBV-coinfection and 14 kg pediatric contrasts against Dovato's boxed warning are standard label reading and well known to HIV clinicians.
verdicts.correction: Lead the product comparison with the v19 to v22 indication change and treat HBV and pediatric coverage as table filler. Tie it to numbers only as share defense ahead of the 2028 negotiated price, not as upside.

overall: Most of Gilead's candidates are already on the record. Management sized the $400M IP revenue and the ~$1.1B Part D headwind on calls and slides, said the price-led Biktarvy drivers on its own Q2 2026 slide, and the IRA spillover language and the MFN repatriation term were already in the FY2024 10-K and in peers' filings. Two candidates hold: the footnote-only $568-638M of Trodelvy inventory on a manufacturing process FDA has not approved (c04), and the quiet August 2025 Biktarvy label widening (c08). c08 is the least obvious, but neither has a large number yet.
